free_tier.stated: Sirius (jh-1c-1g-20gb-nvme) at USD 4.82/month: 1 Intel core shared, 1,024 MB RAM, 20 GB NVMe, 51,200 GB/month and a 0.29 Gbps port as the tracker states them, IPv4 + IPv6, Tirana Albania. The vendor's own plan page contradicts the allowance: it sells "Free unmetered traffic. You only pay for disk space. Every plan includes unlimited traffic." and prices the IPv4 separately at USD 3.31/month, with the free IPv6 address described as the budget path. The page title advertises "VPS from $1.99", which is the provider-wide entry price and not this plan's price.

egress.terms: the plan page claims unlimited traffic and no metering, and sells bandwidth as a port upgrade (USD 2.50 a month for 10 Mbps more, USD 333.33 a month for a dedicated 1 Gbps); the tracker's 51,200 GB a month is not on the vendor page and is not recorded as the vendor's allowance

interface_detail: inferred from the tooling the provider documents; not probed
tooling: KVM with root, SSH access, instant location switching across 80 locations and IP changes from the client area, sold through a configurator; the company is Baxet Group Inc. of Hong Kong and the site states 379,589 customers and 53,131 active VPS.
chaining: 20 GB of NVMe with claimed unlimited traffic and instant location switching is a crawler front end that can be moved when a region is rate-limited
limits_note: the plan page states no byte allowance at all ("Free unmetered traffic ... unlimited traffic") while the tracker lists 51,200 GB a month and a 0.29 Gbps port for the same plan; with an allowance stated only by a third party, the record says none and flags the conflict here rather than choosing the tracker's number as the vendor's.
